title: Allocation window and soft-throttle policy for short-term capacity boosts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Customers on Dedicated fleets occasionally need short-lived extra throughput for traffic spikes (marketing events, nightly jobs, demo load). Today we provide a reserved baseline and a blunt overage model that either bills at a high multiplier or routes to lower-tier models. Operators lack a predictable, controllable mechanism to give small temporary headroom without causing surprise invoices or violating tenant fairness.

Goal: Define and implement an "allocation window" and "soft-throttle" policy that allows tenants to request/receive short-term capacity boosts (minutes-to-hours) with:
- clear, predictable invoicing (pro rata or capped)
- operator-visible state and controls (grant/revoke, telemetry)
- fairness across concurrent boosters to protect baseline SLOs
- integration with autoscaling/autoburst rules and routing fallback

Scope: This ticket covers the policy definition, runtime admission changes, billing signal hooks, operator console surface, and a Canary rollout for a subset of Dedicated fleets. Implementation work split across runtime (admission & throttling), control plane (API + operator UI), and billing (metering tag + invoice rule).

Key constraints and trade-offs considered: 
- Simplicity vs accuracy: Metering per-second headroom is accurate but increases cost and billing complexity. We propose minute-resolution, bucketed metering with explicit cap windows to balance fidelity and cost of accounting.
- Latency vs isolation: To maintain tenant latency SLOs, we limit per-tenant boost share and allow graceful degradation of boosts (soft-throttle to reduced qps) rather than preemptive kill.
- Predictability vs flexibility: We will support two modes: "pre-authorized window" (customer/operator schedules boost) and "on-demand" (ad-hoc requests subject to stricter caps and higher pro-rate).

High-level design proposal: 
1) Allocation Window construct (control plane): "alloc_window" object with fields: start_time, duration_minutes, max_headroom_rps, billing_cap_usd. Created by API/Console or via operator. Windows are recorded in control plane and propagated to fleet scheduler.
2) Soft-throttle admission in runtime: Runtime accepts alloc_window tokens and tags requests from boosted tenants. If aggregate boost demand > available headroom, runtime enters soft-throttle where boosted requests receive token-bucket-shaped reduced capacity (graceful per-request slowdown and admission probability), prioritized by tenant priority and preflight grants.
3) Metering & billing: Requests during allocation windows are tagged with boost_label and aggregated per-window per-tenant at minute granularity. Billing pipeline applies cap/buffer rules and emits a preview charge visible on Console.
4) Operator Console: New "Boosts" tab under Dedicated fleet showing active windows, projected cost, current consumption, and an operator action panel (extend/revoke/scale). Alerts for >80% consumption and conflicts.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Policy documented in Confluence with examples (pre-authorized vs on-demand) and admin playbook.
- Runtime changes admitted and tested in canary cluster with synthetic load demonstrating graceful degradation instead of hard failures.
- Billing pipeline emits tagged metrics and a sample invoice line for a test tenant.
- Console shows live boost state and operator actions.
- No regressions on baseline SLOs for tenants not participating in boosts (latency p99 within 10% of baseline during tests).

Rollout plan: 
- Stage 1 (week 1): Land control-plane schema + console UI behind feature flag. No runtime enforcement.
- Stage 2 (week 2): Runtime acceptance and tagging in canary fleets (internal only). Run synthetic tests, validate tagging and metering.
- Stage 3 (week 3): Billing pipeline integration in staging, confirm invoice preview accuracy.
- Stage 4 (week 4): Gradual rollout to 10% of eligible Dedicated fleets, monitor customer impact metrics, expose opt-in to customers.

Open questions: 
- What default headroom share should be allowed for on-demand windows? Proposal: 10% of fleet capacity or 2x baseline for 15 minutes, whichever smaller.
- Should boost consumption be borrowable across tenants (first-come-first-served) or allocated proportionally? Proposal: proportionally by baseline reservation with an operator-overridable tie-breaker.
- How will discounts/committed capacity contracts interact with boost billing? Billing to implement ruleset that avoids double-charging committed units; boosts should be invoiced as overage only after committed pool is fully consumed.

Related artifacts and references: 
- Confluence design doc (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DED/Allocation+Window+Design
- Billing spec PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/378 (draft)
- Runtime admission PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1021 (WIP)
- Console mockups: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/boost-console-mockups (internal)

comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting held. Agreed on minute-level metering to reduce billing complexity. Decided to prototype as 'alloc_window' in control plane. Action items assigned.

2026-03-11 - Marco Rivera: Initial runtime prototype accepts alloc_window and propagates boost_label in requests. Observed increased metering events; need to add sampling to avoid cardinality explosion.

2026-03-12 - Jules Martin: Billing draft PR created; testing cap logic against historical tenant usage. Noted edge case where short bursts under 2 minutes currently get rounded to 1 minute — will document rounding rule.
2026-03-13 - Leah Gomez: Console mockups reviewed by PMs and operators. Operators requested 'bulk-revoke' and an override password protected action. Design updated.
2026-03-14 - Marco Rivera: Runtime WIP PR opened (link in related artifacts). Implemented soft-throttle using admission probability curve; initial synthetic canary shows non-boosted p99 unaffected.
2026-03-14 - Aisha Patel: Decided to run canary on two low-risk fleets next week. Added wallet-based preview for customers to opt-in.
